posts.text:
Reading me with the Comic makes it funnier. I promise. lol

Somewhere, a hiring manager is trying to order a senior engineer with free shipping and no assembly required.

“Does this one come with judgment?”
“Yes. Someone spent years helping them develop it.”
“Great. Can we remove that part from the invoice?”

Welcome to the pre-trained employee marketplace. Every candidate must arrive knowing the systems, understanding the customers and remembering an incident that happened before they joined.

Ideally, they caused it. That's the kind of ownership we're looking for.

A junior applicant offers to learn.

Unfortunately, learning requires someone who knows things to spend time with someone who doesn't. Finance has identified both participants as a cost.

So the vacancy stays open for nine months. Three senior people cover it. Two postpone their holidays. One starts answering recruiter messages while technically still in the meeting about retention.

Excellent. We have created another experienced candidate for the market.

The recruiter finally finds the perfect person at a competitor. They want a higher salary, a signing bonus and protected time to mentor junior staff.

Could we negotiate away that last bit? It sounds suspiciously like the thing we canceled to afford them.

Then comes the succession-planning workshop.

“Who takes over when our experts leave?”

Everyone studies the org chart as if a new employee might hatch from one of the boxes.

HR suggests developing people internally. The room reacts like someone has proposed making electricity at home with a bicycle.

Training needs real work, feedback and time from people who can teach. Cut all three and you may save this quarter's budget while bidding against everyone else for next year's seniors.

Back at the interview, the graduate has a question.

“Where did your current senior people get their first opportunity?”

A long silence.

“We're very proud of our competitors' graduate programs.”

Introduction At IBM Software, we transform client challenges into solutions. Building the worlds leading AI-powered, cloud-native products that shape the future of business and society. Were rewriting how data moves and what the world can do with it. With Confluent, data doesnt sit still. Our platform puts information in motion, streaming in near real-time so companies can react faster, build smarter, and deliver experiences as dynamic as the world around them. It takes a certain kind of person to join this team. Those who ask hard questions, give honest feedback, and show up for each other. No egos, no solo acts. Just smart, curious humans pushing toward something bigger, together. Senior Software Engineers II at Confluent take ownership of critical backend systems that underpin our data streaming platform. Youll lead the design and delivery of large-scale, distributed services that must be secure, highly available, and easy to operate across regions and clouds. The team owns a highly available, scalable metadata store - the source of truth that services across Confluent Cloud build on. It serves low-latency read and write APIs, and streams data in real time. The platform is a foundational backbone of a broader effort to re-architect Confluent Cloud and replacing bespoke, per-team datastores with a single self-serve platform. Job Title- Jr. Full-Stack Engineer (AI Agent Developer)
Location- NY, NY (Onsite)
Duration- 6+ Months
Interview- In-Person
Visa : H1B, H4EAD, GC,USC

JOB DESCRIPTION
We're looking for a Jr. Full-Stack Engineer (AI Agent Developer) to help build, test, and support enterprise conversational AI agents and the web experiences around them.
You'll work alongside senior engineers on Google Cloud Platform (GECX / Dialogflow CX), connect agents to Azure and ServiceNow, build front-end interfaces, and help maintain the pipelines and tests that keep releases reliable.

Key Responsibilities

Agent and Backend

• Build and test conversational flows, intents, route groups, and LLM-powered tools in GECX / Dialogflow CX.
• Contribute to agents built with Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK).
• Develop and maintain REST APIs, webhooks, and small services using Python, .NET, or Node.js.
• Integrate conversational agents with ServiceNow and Azure systems.
• Write SQL queries for agent lookups, reporting, and conversational analytics.

Front-End Development

• Create responsive and accessible web interfaces using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and TypeScript.
• Work with modern front-end frameworks such as React or Angular.
• Connect front-end components to backend services and agent APIs.
• Implement loading states, error handling, and browser session management.
• Contribute to internal dashboards for agent analytics, test results, and administrative tasks.

Delivery, Testing & Support

• Help maintain Azure DevOps pipelines used to validate and deploy agent configurations, fulfillment services, and front-end builds.
• Update existing YAML pipelines with appropriate review.
• Write and execute unit tests, webhook API tests, Dialogflow regression tests, and front-end component tests.
• Investigate bugs and failed test runs, document findings, and escalate issues when needed.
• Participate in sprint planning, daily standups, backlog refinement, and Program Increment (PI) planning within a SAFe environment.
• Maintain documentation covering flow designs, API behavior, UI components, and operational runbooks.



Tooling & Environment

• Conversational AI & Cloud: Google Cloud Platform (GECX / Dialogflow CX), Microsoft Azure.
• Back End: Python 3.x (Primary), .NET (C#), Node.js, SQL.
• Front End: HTML, CSS, TypeScript / JavaScript, React, Angular.
• DevOps & Testing: Azure DevOps (Pipelines, Repos), Git, API Testing, Unit Testing, UI Testing.

posts.text:
One thing I’ve become more comfortable with over the years is recognizing that not every problem needs a new technology.
As developers, it’s natural to get excited about a new framework, cloud service, architecture pattern, or tool. Learning and experimenting with new technologies is part of what keeps this field interesting.
But experience has taught me that newer doesn’t always mean better.
Sometimes an existing .NET application already has a solid foundation and only needs the right improvements.
Sometimes introducing another microservice adds more complexity than value.
And sometimes improving what we already have is a much better decision than rebuilding everything from scratch.
I still enjoy learning new technologies and keeping up with how software development is evolving. At the same time, I’ve become more thoughtful about where a technology actually adds value to the application and the business.
For me, that’s an important part of growing as a developer.
Good engineering isn’t about using the most technologies. It’s about choosing the right solution and keeping things as simple as they need to be.

The journey continues, and I'm excited to keep learning, building, mentoring, and contributing to meaningful projects that create real business value.
Here's to the next chapter of growth, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Email: korrapatipragathi2709@gmail.com

Introduction At IBM Software, we transform client challenges into solutions. Building the worlds leading AI-powered, cloud-native products that shape the future of business and society. It takes a certain kind of person to join this team. Those who ask hard questions, give honest feedback, and show up for each other. No egos, no solo acts. Just smart, curious humans pushing toward something bigger, together. Senior Software Engineers II at Confluent take ownership of critical backend systems that underpin our data streaming platform. Youll lead the design and delivery of large-scale, distributed services that must be secure, highly available, and easy to operate across regions and clouds. The team owns a highly available, scalable metadata store - the source of truth that services across Confluent Cloud build on. It serves low-latency read and write APIs, and streams data in real time. The platform is a foundational backbone of a broader effort to re-architect Confluent Cloud and replacing bespoke, per-team datastores with a single self-serve platform. Responsibilities - Build and evolve the metadata platform - the read, write, and streaming APIs - Solve hard distributed-systems problems - availability, consistency, sharding, scaling - Design, build, and operate resilient, scalable systems across a stack spanning multiple clouds and services - Independently drive projects - spot high-impact gap Required Skills 6+ years of industry experience designing, building, and operating large-scale backend services in production Strong programming and algorithmic skills, with proficiency in a major language

JD :
 
We are seeking a Python Fullstack Lead with deep expertise in Python, distributed systems, cloud-native architecture, and microservices. The candidate must have in-depth expertise in at least one major cloud platform — AWS, Azure, or GCP and the ability to translate business requirements into scalable, resilient, secure, and production-ready architectures. • Python 3.x, FastAPI/Flask/Django, asyncio, concurrency, type hints, testing, profiling and performance optimization.

• Experience working with AI tools would be a plus
• Experience with retail/e-commerce, high-volume transaction processing, multi-region architectures.
• Strong understanding of system design, distributed systems, scalability, resilience, security and production operations

We’re hiring at Sermo, and both roles are remote across the US and Latin America.

Forward Deployed AI Engineer, Delivery and Operations:

Redesign real business workflows around AI agents and ship them to production, not prototypes. You’ll embed with our delivery and operations teams, map how work actually gets done, and build agents with human approval, evaluation and monitoring built in. Python, C#/.NET, React and Salesforce are part of the day to day. Professional Spanish is required.

Senior Software Engineer:

Own features from the database to the browser in our ASP.NET Core and React platforms, and use AI coding agents like Claude Code every day. You’ll write the specs, direct the agents, review what they produce and own what ships. We want 7+ years building complex web apps, deep experience on either the .NET or React side, and real fluency in the other.

Sermo is the largest online community of physicians in the world, and the work here helps doctors collaborate and gets better insights to the people who care for patients. We care less about titles and more about what you’ve shipped, who used it, and what changed because of it.
